transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is rejecting impeachment articles introduced against him
yesterday by outgoing Republican Congressman Thomas Massie.
These accuse Hegseth of mishandling the war in Iran.
Hegseth says using impeachment as a tool to force him out is inappropriate.
The history is clear and it's very straightforward.
And one disgruntled congressman wants to shred it over policy disagreements.
That's what it is, policy disagreements.
Not high crimes, not misdemeanors, not treason, not bribery, not the kinds of offenses the
founders intended when they wrote the impeachment clause.
Writing online, a short time ago, President Trump says Hegseth gets an A plus plus plus
against Congressman Massie, whom he calls a "loser."
The president says Gulf Arab allies do not want the U.S. and Israel to attack Iran again.
He met Qatar's prime minister yesterday at the White House, and P.E.R.'s Aya Betrawi
has more.
Qatar's foreign ministry says the country's prime minister had a "positive" closed-door
meeting at the White House on Monday with Trump and Vice President Vance about the latest
efforts to resolve the crisis between Washington and Tehran.
Qatar says it will continue working to bridge the divide between the U.S. and Iran, indicating
there is still no breakthrough to the stalemate.
Trump wrote online after the meeting that an attack on Iran at this point, in his words,
seems to be quite unlikely.
He says there's positive momentum to ending the conflict.
Iran, however, has several demands for restarting nuclear talks.
They include the U.S. unfreezing billions in overseas accounts and lifting its naval
blockade to export oil again.
Aya Betrawi, NPR News, Dubai.
The suspect accused of killing conservative activist Charlie Kirk last year at a Utah
college now has a trial date from member station KUER Hugo Ricard Bell reports.
June 21, 2028.
That's when jury selection will begin in Tyler Robinson's trial, Fourth District Judge Tony
Graff ruled.
This trial setting and case management order's intent is to ensure that the constitutional
rights of Mr. Robinson and Mrs. Kirk are upheld at every junction.
District's widow Erica requested a speedy trial several times.
In court, her attorney Jeffrey Nyman told Judge Graff that the trial date he set was
not appropriate.
A trial in the summer of 2028, three years after Charlie's assassination, does not feel
very speedy to the Kirk family.
Robinson has pleaded not guilty to seven charges, including aggravated murder, which can carry
the death penalty.
For NPR News, I'm Hugo Ricard Bell in Provo, Utah.
The federal government says that consumer prices rose four-tenths of one percent in
October.
That's a little less than they were in September.
You're listening to NPR News.
Health officials in Pennsylvania say they have confirmed more than 1,500 cases of the
measles in that state.
There are several new cases that were identified in the past few days.
Earlier, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported that, across the country,
more than 5,000 cases of measles have been reported.
The Food and Drug Administration is requiring drug makers to add a new warning to the labels
of popular GLP-1 drugs.
NPR's Sydney Lupkin reports it's about a rare eye condition that can lead to permanent
vision loss.
The FDA says there's potentially an increased risk of a rare eye problem associated with
GLP-1 medications.
It's called non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, or NION, and it's caused
by decreased blood flow to the optic nerve.
The condition is usually painless and results in vision loss in one eye that can be permanent.
The FDA is requiring drug companies making GLP-1s to add information about NION to the
warning sections of their labels.
GLP-1 drugs include Ozimpic and Wagovie, as well as Manjaro, Zepbond and Foundeo.
They also include drugs like Trulicity and Victoza.
Patients should be aware of the risk and contact their doctors right away if they experience
vision symptoms while taking these drugs.
Sydney Lupkin, NPR News.
This year's Booker Prize in fiction has been awarded.
The winner is British writer M. John Harrison.
He's been honored for his science fiction novel, The End of Everything, the novel features
themes of apocalypse.
You're listening to NPR.
This message comes from VCU.

It's knowledge put to work.
VCU scholars and researchers are expanding what's known and what's possible across
health, science, engineering, the arts, and more.
It's the kind of work that places VCU among the nation's top 50 public research universities.
Virginia Commonwealth University, a world unlike any other.
Learn more at VCU.edu.

topics.text: Hegseth rejects Massie's impeachment articles over Iran war, calling them policy disagreements
Trump praises Hegseth and calls Massie a loser; Gulf allies oppose renewed Iran attack
Qatar's prime minister holds positive White House meeting with Trump and Vance on Iran crisis
Tyler Robinson's trial for Charlie Kirk killing set to begin June 21, 2028
Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, slightly less than September's increase
Pennsylvania confirms over 1,500 measles cases; US total tops 5,000
FDA requires warning on GLP-1 drug labels about rare eye condition causing vision loss
British writer M. John Harrison wins Booker Prize for science fiction novel The End of Everything
